docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
Dependencies are managed using the [pip-tools] tool chain.

Unpinned dependencies are specified in pyproject.toml. Pinned versions are then produced with:

pip-compile pyproject.toml

To add/remove packages edit pyproject.toml and run the above command. To upgrade all existing dependencies run:

pip-compile --upgrade pyproject.toml

Dependencies for developers are listed separately as optional, with the pinned versions being saved to dev-requirements.txt instead.

pip-tools can also manage these dependencies by adding extra arguments, e.g.:

pip-compile -o dev-requirements.txt --extra=dev pyproject.toml

When dependencies are upgraded, both requirements.txt and dev-requirements.txt should be regenerated so that they are in sync.

docs.title: Bundling Solidity GUI as an executable
docs.text:
Solidity GUI can be bundled as an executable using [pyinstaller].

To do this, you first have to install the dependencies in dev-requirements.txt, as described above. Next you need to run:

pyinstaller Solidity-GUI.spec

This should create a single executable file in the dist/ folder.

docs.title: User Input via Forms
docs.text:
We often need to gather data from the user that is:

  • structured - has pre-determined named fields
  • typed - e.g. numbers rather than strings
  • validated - has been checked for correctness

Cases that meet these criteria should make of use the Forms module. The reference documentation for the module provides an introduction to its design, functionality and usage.

The Forms module is still in an early stage of development so it's expected that it will have to be extended to suit future use-cases. Please note that if the Forms module does not currently address your use-case you are strongly recommended to consider extending it rather than implementing custom code for an individual form. In particular, the following current limitations are noted:

  • Limited range of fields and widgets available.
  • No ability to specify default values for fields.
  • No nesting of forms.
  • No inter-field dependencies - e.g. checking a box to another field available

Implementing additional field and widget classes will probably be the most common extension and should be relatively straightforward based on the existing examples.

Solidity-GUI is a software for preparing system geometries in a mesh format for use by the Solidity tool.

Run the software with: python -m solidity_gui.

def run() -> None:
"""Main entry point to program."""
    import multiprocessing
    import sys

    from . import solidity  # noqa
    from .initialise import initialise_app

    initialise_app()

    if sys.platform == "linux":
        import os

        # Force Qt to use X11 backend, even if we're running on Wayland, as VTK requires
        # it
        os.environ["QT_QPA_PLATFORM"] = "xcb"

    # Needed if you're using multiprocessing within a pyinstaller-built exe on Windows,
    # otherwise your main window will repeatedly open
    multiprocessing.freeze_support()

    # NB: We import PySide *after* setting QT_QPA_PLATFORM
    from PySide6.QtWidgets import QApplication

    from .main.main_window import MainWindow

    app = QApplication()
    window = MainWindow()
    window.show()
    app.exec()

def initialise_logging(process_name: str | None) -> None:
"""Configure the program's logger.

    Args:
      process_name: applied as a suffix to the logging filename if provided
    """
    log_path = user_log_path(config.APP_NAME.replace(" ", "-"), config.APP_AUTHOR)
    log_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    suffix = f"-process-{process_name}" if process_name else ""
    filename = log_path / (
        f"{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d_%H-%M-%S')}" + suffix + ".log"
    )

    # Log to console and file
    logging.basicConfig(
        level=logging.INFO,
        format="%(asctime)s [%(levelname)s] %(message)s",
        handlers=[logging.FileHandler(filename), logging.StreamHandler()],
        force=True,  # make sure config is applied in background processes
    )

    logging.info(f"Saving log to {filename}")

def get_assignments_for_mesh(
    self, mesh: Mesh
) -> dict[str, list[ConditionAssignment]]:
"""Returns all ConditionAssignments associated with a particular mesh."""
    assignments: dict[str, list[ConditionAssignment]] = dict()
    for assignment in self.values():
        if assignment.cell_set_name in mesh.cell_sets:
            # should only ever be one cell type in a cell set
            cell_type = list(mesh.cell_sets_dict[assignment.cell_set_name].keys())[
                0
            ]
            assignments.setdefault(cell_type, []).append(assignment)
    return assignments

def get_joined_volumes(volumes: list[Dummy]) -> list[tuple[Dummy, Dummy]]:
"""Detect the shared surfaces between a set of volumes in the active gmsh model.

    Args:
      volumes: the volumes to check
    """
    surface_tags = [
        list(gmsh.model.occ.get_surface_loops(vol._id)[1][0]) for vol in volumes
    ]
    repeated_surface_tags = [
        item for item, count in Counter(chain(*surface_tags)).items() if count > 1
    ]

    shared_surfaces = []
    for tag in repeated_surface_tags:
        volume_tags = [i for i, surface in enumerate(surface_tags) if tag in surface]
        if len(volume_tags) != 2:
            raise ValueError("Error detecting shared surfaces in geometry.")
        joined_volumes = (volumes[volume_tags[0]], volumes[volume_tags[1]])
        if (
            joined_volumes not in shared_surfaces
            and joined_volumes[::-1] not in shared_surfaces
        ):
            shared_surfaces.append(joined_volumes)
    return shared_surfaces

def load_geometry(parent: QWidget) -> None:
"""Load and a new geometry into a GmshProcess and display the resulting mesh."""
    filename, _ = QFileDialog.getOpenFileName(
        parent,
        caption="Select gmsh geometry file",
        filter="GMSH geometry (*.geo *.step *.brep)",
    )
    if not filename:
        return

    form_dialog = GeometryNameDialog(GeometryNameForm)
    form_dialog.setWindowTitle("Set Component Name")
    try:
        form_data = form_dialog.run()
    except ValueError:
        return

    geom_name = form_data["name"]

    if geom_name in gmsh_process_datastore:
        display_error_message("A component with that name already exists.")
        return

    # assert geom_name not in gmsh_process_datastore
    gmsh_process = GmshProcess(geom_name)
    gmsh_process.start()
    gmsh_process_datastore[geom_name] = gmsh_process

    logging.info(f"Importing geometry from file: {filename}")
    mesh = gmsh_process.call_function(
        "import_geometry", geom_name=geom_name, filename=filename
    )
    pub.sendMessage("add_component.finish", mesh_name=geom_name, obj=mesh)

def get_by_materials(
    self, material1: Material, material2: Material
) -> JointInterfaceMaterial:
"""Retrieve a joint interface materials using its consituent materials.

    Args:
      material1: first material of the interface
      material2: second material of the interface
    """
    for key, joint_material in self.items():
        if (
            material1 == joint_material.material1
            and material2 == joint_material.material2
        ) or (
            material2 == joint_material.material1
            and material1 == joint_material.material2

    raise ValueError(

def get_joint_material_interfaces(
    gmsh_processes: Datastore[str, GmshProcess],
    material_assignments: MaterialAssignmentDatastore,
) -> list[tuple[Material, Material]]:
"""Find all interfaces between different materials that have joint elements.

    Args:
      gmsh_processes: all gmsh processes containing relevant geometric data
      material_assignments: material assignment information
    """
    joined_materials = []

    for gmsh_process in gmsh_processes.values():
        joined_volume_names = gmsh_process.call_function("get_joined_volumes")

        if not is_iterable_of_2uple_of_string(joined_volume_names):
            raise ValueError("Expected Iterable[tuple[str, str]]")
        for volume_name1, volume_name2 in joined_volume_names:
            try:
                _, assignment1 = material_assignments.get_by_cell_set_name(volume_name1)
                _, assignment2 = material_assignments.get_by_cell_set_name(volume_name2)
            except ValueError:
                continue
            if (
                not assignment1.material.properties["joint"].enabled
                or not assignment2.material.properties["joint"].enabled
            ):
                continue
            joined_material = (assignment1.material, assignment2.material)

            if (
                joined_material not in joined_materials
                and joined_material[::-1] not in joined_materials
            ):
                joined_materials.append(joined_material)
    return joined_materials

"""Type guard checking  return type from a get_jointed_volumes function call."""
    if not isinstance(iterable, Iterable):

    for data in iterable:

        for val in data:
            if not isinstance(val, str):

    return True

Calculate the offset applied to indices of a cell_type for a mesh.

The indices return by gmsh for cells (elements) are offset by the total number of cells of lower dimension present in the mesh. For instance, if a mesh has two vertices the indices for lines will start at 2. If the mesh also has 3 lines then the indices for triangles will start at 5 and so on. We often want the map from this indexing system to one in which each of the cell types are indexed independently. The offset value return by this function can be used for this.

def get_cell_offset(cells_dict: dict[str, np.ndarray], cell_type: str) -> int:
"""Calculate the offset applied to indices of a cell_type for a mesh.

    The indices return by gmsh for cells (elements) are offset by the total number of
    cells of lower dimension present in the mesh. For instance, if a mesh has two
    vertices the indices for lines will start at 2. If the mesh also has 3 lines then
    the indices for triangles will start at 5 and so on. We often want the map from this
    indexing system to one in which each of the cell types are indexed
    independently. The offset value return by this function can be used for this.

    Args:
      cells_dict: the cell data from the mesh
      cell_type: the type of cell for which we want the offset
    """
    offset = 0
    for type_ in ("vertex", "line", "triangle"):
        if cell_type == type_:
            break
        offset += cells_dict[type_].shape[0]
    return offset

    filename, _ = QFileDialog.getOpenFileName(
        parent,
        caption="Select a session file",
        filter="Session files (*.pickle)",

    if not filename:
        return

        for mesh_name, mesh in mesh_datastore.items():

            gmsh_process.start()

            _ = gmsh_process.call_function(

                filename=f"{session_name}_{mesh_name}.brep",
            )
            gmsh_process.call_function(
                "merge_mesh", filename=f"{session_name}_{mesh_name}.msh"

def save_session(parent: QWidget) -> None:
"""Save the current session to a file."""
    session_filename, _ = QFileDialog.getSaveFileName(
        parent,
        caption="Save session",
        filter="Session files (*.pickle)",
    )

    # If extension not given, automatically add it
    if not session_filename.endswith(".pickle"):
        session_filename += ".pickle"

    with open(session_filename, "wb") as session_file:
        pickle.dump(
            {
                "meshes": mesh_datastore,
                "material_assignments": material_assignment_datastore,
                "materials": material_datastore,
                "condition_assignments": condition_assignment_datastore,
                "conditions": condition_datastore,
                "initial_condition_assignments": initial_condition_assignment_datastore,
                "initial_conditions": initial_condition_datastore,
                "controls": control_datastore,
            },
            session_file,
        )

    session_name = Path(session_filename).parent / Path(session_filename).stem
    for mesh_name, gmsh_process in gmsh_process_datastore.items():
        for extension in ["brep", "msh"]:
            gmsh_process.call_function(
                "write_file",
                filename=f"{session_name}_{mesh_name}.{extension}",
            )

def fetch_condition_assignments(
    mesh: Mesh,
    conditions: ConditionDatastore,
    condition_assignments: ConditionAssignmentDatastore,
) -> np.ndarray:
"""Fetch the condition assignments for a given mesh."""
    node_count = mesh.points.shape[0]
    node_assignments = np.array(
        (np.arange(node_count), np.full(node_count, -1)), dtype="int64"
    ).T
    # important that we work on the cell types in this order so that lower dimension
    # entities take precedence over higher dimension
    cell_type_order = ("tetra", "triangle")
    mesh_assignments = condition_assignments.get_assignments_for_mesh(mesh)
    for cell_type in cell_type_order:
        if cell_type not in mesh_assignments:
            continue
        for assignment in mesh_assignments[cell_type]:
            cell_set = mesh.cell_sets_dict[assignment.cell_set_name][cell_type]
            cell_id_offset = get_cell_offset(mesh.cells_dict, cell_type)
            cell_ids = cell_set - cell_id_offset
            node_ids = np.unique(mesh.cells_dict[cell_type][cell_ids].flatten())
            condition_id = conditions.get_positional_index(assignment.condition)
            node_assignments[node_ids, 1] = condition_id
    return node_assignments

    materials: MaterialDatastore,
    material_assignments: Mapping[int, MaterialAssignment],
) -> np.ndarray:
"""Fetches the material assignments for a given mesh."""
    cell_materials_list = []
    for assignment in material_assignments.values():
        if assignment.cell_set_name in mesh.cell_sets_dict:
            cell_ids = mesh.cell_sets_dict[assignment.cell_set_name]["tetra"]
            material_id = materials.get_positional_index(assignment.material)
            cell_materials_list.append(
                np.array(
                    [
                        cell_ids,
                        np.full_like(cell_ids, material_id),
                    ]
                ).T
            )

    if cell_materials_list:
        cell_materials = np.concatenate(cell_materials_list, axis=0)
    else:
        cell_materials = np.empty((0, 2), dtype="uint64")

    return cell_materials

def generate_elements_data(
    meshes: Mapping[str, Mesh],
    materials: MaterialDatastore,
    material_assignments: Mapping[int, MaterialAssignment],
    surface_nodes: Mapping[str, np.ndarray],
) -> ElementData:
"""Generates the elements section data for the Solidity input file."""
    points_per_tetra = 4
    all_node_ids = np.empty((0, points_per_tetra + 1), dtype="uint64")
    boundary_tetra = np.empty((0,), dtype="uint64")

    node_id_offset = 0

    cell_materials_sorted = np.empty((0, 2), dtype="uint64")
    cell_id_offset = 0

    total_tetra = sum(
        mesh.cells_dict["tetra"].data.shape[0] for mesh in meshes.values()
    )

    for i, (mesh_name, mesh) in enumerate(meshes.items()):
        cell_materials = fetch_material_assignments(
            mesh, materials, material_assignments
        )
        check_unassigned_cells(cell_materials, mesh)

        cell_materials[:, 0] += cell_id_offset

        cell_materials_sorted = np.concatenate(
            (
                cell_materials_sorted,
                cell_materials[cell_materials[:, 0].argsort()],
            )
        )
        cell_id_offset += cell_materials.shape[0]

        # We can now get the node ids for each cell, offset by the accumulated number of
        # nodes from previous meshes
        node_ids = mesh.cells_dict["tetra"]

        # Find the indices of tetra elements that contain surface nodes
        indices = np.where(
            np.apply_along_axis(
                lambda x: np.isin(x[:4], surface_nodes[mesh_name]).any(),
                1,
                node_ids,
            )
        )[0]
        boundary_tetra_layer = np.zeros(node_ids.shape[0], dtype="uint64")
        boundary_tetra_layer[indices] = i + 1
        boundary_tetra = np.concatenate(
            (
                boundary_tetra,
                boundary_tetra_layer,
            )
        )

        # Append the mesh ID to each row
        mesh_ids = np.full(
            (mesh.cells_dict["tetra"].shape[0], 1), i + 1, dtype="uint64"
        )
        node_ids = np.concatenate((node_ids + node_id_offset, mesh_ids), axis=1)

        all_node_ids = np.concatenate((all_node_ids, node_ids), axis=0)

        node_id_offset += mesh.points.shape[0]

    return dict(
        num_tetra=total_tetra,
        points_per_tetra=points_per_tetra,
        cell_materials=cell_materials_sorted[:, 1],
        tetra_node_ids=all_node_ids,
        boundary_tetra=boundary_tetra,
        num_meshes=len(meshes),
    )

def generate_material_data(materials: Mapping[int, Material]) -> dict[str, Any]:
"""Generates data for the material properties section of the input file."""
    property_lines: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for i, material in enumerate(materials.values(), 1):
        for property_label, property_ in material.properties.items():
            property_line_dict = property_lines.setdefault(property_label, {})
            property_data = (
                property_.data if property_.enabled else property_.default_data
            )
            if property_data is None:
                raise SystemValidationError(
                    f"Has not been set for the property '{property_.name}' of material "
                    f"'{material.name}'."
                )
            for key, value in property_data.items():
                property_line_dict.setdefault(key, []).append(value)
        calculated_properties = property_lines.setdefault("_calculated", {})
        calculated_properties.setdefault("is_joint", []).append(13)
        calculated_properties.setdefault("is_fracture", []).append(
            3 if material.properties["joint"].enabled else 0
        )
        calculated_properties.setdefault("material_index", []).append(i)

    # add in additional copies of materials with joint elements
    extra_materials = 0
    for i, material in enumerate(materials.values()):
        if not material.properties["joint"].enabled:
            continue
        extra_materials += 1
        for property_label, property_ in material.properties.items():
            property_line_dict = property_lines[property_label]
            for property_line in property_line_dict.values():
                property_line.append(property_line[i])
        property_lines["_calculated"]["is_joint"].append(15)
        property_lines["_calculated"]["is_fracture"].append(0)
        property_lines["_calculated"]["material_index"].append(i + 1)
    return dict(
        materials=materials.values(),
        num_materials=len(materials) + extra_materials,
        material_properties=property_lines,
    )

def generate_nodes_data(
    meshes: Mapping[str, Mesh],
    surface_nodes: Mapping[str, np.ndarray],
    conditions: ConditionDatastore,
    condition_assignments: ConditionAssignmentDatastore,
    initial_conditions: InitialConditionDatastore,
    initial_condition_assignments: InitialConditionAssignmentDatastore,
) -> dict[str, object]:
"""Prepare data needed for template renderering."""
    num_nodes = sum(mesh.points.shape[0] for mesh in meshes.values())
    all_nodes = np.concatenate([mesh.points for mesh in meshes.values()], axis=0)

    combined_surface_nodes = np.array([])
    incr = 0
    all_node_conditions = np.empty((0, 2), dtype="int64")
    all_node_initial_conditions = np.empty((0, 3))
    for mesh_name in meshes:
        mesh_surface_nodes = surface_nodes[mesh_name]
        mesh_surface_nodes = mesh_surface_nodes + incr
        combined_surface_nodes = np.concatenate(
            [combined_surface_nodes, mesh_surface_nodes]
        )

        mesh_node_conditions = fetch_condition_assignments(
            meshes[mesh_name], conditions, condition_assignments
        )
        check_unassigned_nodes(mesh_node_conditions, meshes[mesh_name])

        mesh_node_conditions[:, 0] += incr
        all_node_conditions = np.concatenate(
            (all_node_conditions, mesh_node_conditions)
        )

        mesh_node_initial_conditions = fetch_initial_conditions(
            meshes[mesh_name], initial_conditions, initial_condition_assignments
        )
        all_node_initial_conditions = np.concatenate(
            (all_node_initial_conditions, mesh_node_initial_conditions)
        )

        incr += meshes[mesh_name].points.shape[0]

    surface_node_flags = np.zeros((num_nodes,), dtype="uint64")
    surface_node_flags[combined_surface_nodes.astype("uint64")] = 1

    return dict(
        num_nodes=num_nodes,
        nodes=all_nodes,
        surface_node_flags=surface_node_flags,
        node_conditions=all_node_conditions[:, 1],
        node_initial_conditions=all_node_initial_conditions,
    )

    joint_material_interfaces: Iterable[tuple[Material, Material]],
    joint_materials: JointMaterialDatastore,
    materials: MaterialDatastore,
) -> dict[str, object]:
"""Get the data needed to render the mat file template."""
    joint_material_data: list[JointMaterialData] = []
    for material_id, material in enumerate(materials.values()):
        if material.properties["joint"].enabled:
            other = material.properties["other"]
            other_data = other.data if other.enabled else other.default_data
            if other_data is None:
                raise SystemValidationError(
                    f"Values have not been set for the property 'other' of "
                    f"material '{material.name}'."
                )
            joint_material_data.append(
                JointMaterialData(
                    index1=material_id,
                    index2=material_id,
                    data=dict(
                        tensile_strength=other_data["tensile_strength"],
                        internal_friction_coefficient=other_data[
                            "internal_friction_coefficient"
                        ],
                        cohesion=other_data["cohesion"],
                        energy_release_rate_mode_1=other_data[
                            "energy_release_rate_mode_1"
                        ],
                        energy_release_rate_mode_2=other_data[
                            "energy_release_rate_mode_2"
                        ],
                    ),
                )
            )
    for material1, material2 in joint_material_interfaces:
        try:
            joint_properties = joint_materials.get_by_materials(
                material1, material2
            ).properties
        except ValueError:
            raise SystemValidationError(
                "Joint material properties have not been set for the interface between "
                f"the materials '{material1.name}' and '{material2.name}'"
            )
        joint_material_data.append(
            JointMaterialData(
                index1=materials.get_positional_index(material1),
                index2=materials.get_positional_index(material2),
                data=joint_properties,
            )
        )
    return dict(
        num_materials=len(joint_material_data), joint_materials=joint_material_data
    )

def get_template_data(
    meshes: Mapping[str, Mesh],
    materials: MaterialDatastore,
    material_assignments: Mapping[int, MaterialAssignment],
    conditions: ConditionDatastore,
    condition_assignments: ConditionAssignmentDatastore,
    initial_conditions: InitialConditionDatastore,
    initial_condition_assignments: InitialConditionAssignmentDatastore,
    control_parameters: Mapping[str, object],
    surface_nodes: Mapping[str, np.ndarray],
) -> dict[str, object]:
"""Get the data needed to render the input file template."""
    data: dict[str, object] = {}
    element_data = generate_elements_data(
        meshes, materials, material_assignments, surface_nodes
    )
    data.update(element_data)
    data.update(generate_interactions_data(meshes))
    data.update(
        generate_nodes_data(
            meshes,
            surface_nodes,
            conditions,
            condition_assignments,
            initial_conditions,
            initial_condition_assignments,
        )
    )
    data.update(generate_material_data(materials))
    data.update(
        dict(
            conditions=conditions.values(),
            num_conditions=len(conditions),
        )
    )
    surface_element_data = generate_surface_elements_data(meshes)
    data.update(surface_element_data)
    num_triangles = surface_element_data["num_triangles"]
    num_joint_elements = (
        ((element_data["num_tetra"] * 4) - num_triangles) // 2
    ) + num_triangles
    data.update(dict(num_joint_elements=num_joint_elements))
    data.update(control_parameters)
    return data

def get_tetra_side_lengths(meshes: Mapping[str, Mesh]) -> np.ndarray:
"""Gets the side lengths of the tetrahedra in the mesh."""
    # this is only good for linear meshes
    # it is probably too memory/compute intensive for large meshes
    # gmsh will release a built in way to do this in the 4.12 release
    # https://gitlab.onelab.info/gmsh/gmsh/-/blob/0dacd204c5b936efdfb9341fd71cabbb06ebb9e2/api/gmsh.py#L2989

    lengths = np.array([])
    for mesh in meshes.values():
        pairings = np.empty((0, 2), dtype="uint64")
        for cell in mesh.cells_dict["tetra"]:
            edges = np.array(list(combinations(cell, 2)))
            pairings = np.concatenate([pairings, edges], axis=0)

        pairings = np.unique(pairings, axis=0)

        dist_vectors = mesh.points[pairings[:, 0]] - mesh.points[pairings[:, 1]]
        lengths = np.concatenate((lengths, np.linalg.norm(dist_vectors, axis=1)))
    return lengths

def render_mesh(self, mesh_name: str, mesh: Mesh) -> None:
"""Render a mesh within the VTKWindow.

    Args:
      mesh_name: The name of the mesh
      mesh: The mesh to render
    """
    logging.info("Rendering mesh")

    ugrid = vtk.vtkUnstructuredGrid()

    points = vtk.vtkPoints()
    for p in mesh.points:
        points.InsertNextPoint(p)
    ugrid.SetPoints(points)

    cellArray = vtk.vtkCellArray()
    for point_ids in mesh.cells_dict["tetra"]:
        tetra = vtk.vtkTetra()
        for i, point_id in enumerate(point_ids):
            tetra.GetPointIds().SetId(i, point_id)
        cellArray.InsertNextCell(tetra)
    ugrid.SetCells(VTK_TETRA, cellArray)

    self.ugrids[mesh_name] = ugrid
    # Create the LUT for scalars to colors
    lut = vtk.vtkLookupTable()
    lut.SetNumberOfTableValues(2)
    lut.SetTableRange(self.unselected_lookup_value, self.selected_lookup_value)
    lut.Build()
    lut.SetTableValue(self.unselected_lookup_value, *config.MESH_COLOUR)
    lut.SetTableValue(self.selected_lookup_value, *config.MESH_SELECTION_COLOUR)

    mapper = vtk.vtkDataSetMapper()
    mapper.SetInputData(ugrid)
    mapper.UseLookupTableScalarRangeOn()
    mapper.SetLookupTable(lut)

    if mesh_name in self.actors:
        self.ren.RemoveActor(self.actors[mesh_name])

    actor = vtk.vtkActor()
    actor.SetMapper(mapper)
    actor.GetProperty().EdgeVisibilityOn()
    self.ren.AddActor(actor)
    self.actors[mesh_name] = actor

    self.ren.ResetCamera()
    self.iren.ReInitialize()
    pub.sendMessage("mesh.rendered", mesh=mesh)

def reorient_camera(self, orientation_vector: Vector, up_vector: Vector) -> None:
"""Updates camera position to a new orientation whilst preserving focal point.

    Args:
        orientation_vector: new orientation w.r.t focal point. Passing a unit vector
                            will preserve the current distance from the focal point.

    focal_point = np.array(camera.GetFocalPoint())

Module for acquiring data from user via forms.

This module aims to provide:

  • a simple, declarative approach to specifying structured data to gather from the user.
  • powerful and flexible validation of data with reporting of human-readable errors.
  • integration with the GUI framework to support rendering of appropriate input and informational components for data collection.

Using this module, creating a dialog box to gather data from the user is as simple as:

class MyForm(Form):
    name = StrField(description="Your full name")
    age = IntField(display_name="Total Age", validators=[Range(min=0)])

dialog = SimpleFormDialog(form_class=MyForm)

This carries out the following:

  • Creates a QDialog displaying a form with two fields and 'OK' and 'Cancel' buttons.
  • Renders each field with a header, optional description text and error message.
  • Applies different styling to the headers, descriptions and error messages.
  • Provides a QLineEdit for the name data and QSpinBox for the age data.
  • Limits the values that can be entered into the QSpinBox widget according to the provided Range validator.
  • Validates provided data when OK is clicked and displays human readable error messages back to the user in the case of validation failure.

For further information, please see:

  • The forms submodule for details on creating Form objects.
  • The fields submodule for details of the available Field types.
  • The dialog submodule for Form rendering and display.
  • The widgets submodule for details of the GUI widgets used in Forms.

This class is designed to be extensible and indeed must be extended to in order to do anything useful. The _ok_clicked handler provides sensible default behaviour in the case of invalid data being provided but does not do anything in the case of valid data.

The simplest intended use case for this form is therefore as below:

class FunctionalDialog(SimpleFormDialog):
    def _ok_clicked(self):
        if data := super()._ok_clicked():
            # do something useful with data

This preserves the data validation behaviour and tacks on additional actions to perform with data that passes validation. Alternatively, you can overwrite _ok_clicked without calling the superclass implementation. This gives more flexibility but you will probably need to implement data validation and form update behaviours.

A basic StyleSheet is applied that assumes the naming conventions used by default_form_renderer. The headers of fields in top-level forms are shown in bold and without bolding for nested fields.

      include_header: whether to render field_info.header in a QLabel

    layout = QVBoxLayout()
    if include_header and field_info.header:
        layout.addWidget(
            _create_named_label(f"{field_info.header.capitalize()}:", f"header-{level}")
        )
    if field_info.description:
        layout.addWidget(_create_named_label(field_info.description, "description"))

    for i, input_ in enumerate(field_info.input):
        if isinstance(field_info.errors, dict):
            if errors := field_info.errors.get(i, None):
                for error in errors:
                    layout.addWidget(_create_named_label(error, "error"))
        layout.addWidget(input_)
    if isinstance(field_info.errors, list):
        for error in field_info.errors:
            layout.addWidget(_create_named_label(error, "error"))
    return layout

def default_form_renderer(form_info: FormInfo, level: int = 0) -> QLayout:
"""Render a FormInfo instance into a QVBoxLayout.

    This function aims to provide a sensible default layout agnostic to use
    context. Field errors, headers and descriptions are displayed as QLabel objects with
    appropriate ObjectName values to allow simple and consistent styling. Errors are
    displayed immediately after the most relevant context (e.g. input widget for field
    level errors, end of form for schema level errors).

    Rendering of nested forms is supported. The level of nesting is tracked via `level`
    and is used to set different ObjectNames for field headers i.e. the QLabel's used to
    display header information at the outer level have the ObjectName 'header-0', at the
    first level of nesting 'header-1' and so on. This can be used in combination with
    the StyleSheet of a dialog to control the appearance of headers at different
    levels. Nested forms are also rendered with a small indent on the left.

    Args:
      form_info: description of the form to render
      level: the level of nesting of the form to render used to fine tune appearance
    """
    layout = QVBoxLayout()

    for info in form_info.fields.values():
        if isinstance(info, FieldInfo):
            layout.addLayout(default_field_renderer(info, level))
        elif isinstance(info, FormInfo):
            if info.header:
                layout.addWidget(
                    _create_named_label(
                        f"{info.header.capitalize()}:", f"header-{level}"
                    )
                )
            if info.single_choice:
                nested_layout = single_choice_form_renderer(info, level + 1)
            else:
                nested_layout = default_form_renderer(info, level + 1)
                # add to left margin to indent nested forms a bit
                margins = nested_layout.getContentsMargins()
                nested_layout.setContentsMargins(margins[0] + 20, *margins[1:])
            layout.addLayout(nested_layout)

    for error in form_info.schema_errors:
        layout.addWidget(_create_named_label(error, "error"))
    return layout

    field_info: FieldInfo, level: int, checked: bool = False

"""Return layout of a form field with an associated radio button.

    Rather than using a QLabel for the header a radio button is used instead. The
    disabled attribute of the field_info object is set according to the checked status
    of the radio button.

    layout = QVBoxLayout()
    radio = QRadioButton(field_info.header)

    field_info.enabled = checked
    field_layout = default_field_renderer(field_info, level, include_header=False)

    def _toggled_handler(checked: bool) -> None:
        field_info.enabled = checked

    radio.toggled.connect(_toggled_handler)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]

    radio.setChecked(checked)
    layout.addWidget(radio)
    layout.addLayout(field_layout)
    return layout

def single_choice_form_renderer(form_info: FormInfo, level: int = 0) -> QLayout:
"""Render a FormInfo instance such that only a single field may be completed.

    This is used to present the user with a choice between data to provide. Practically
    this is achieved via the use of a QGroupBox widget with exclusive radio buttons for
    each field in `form_info`.

    The presence of nested forms is not currently supported.
    """
    layout = QVBoxLayout()
    group_box = QGroupBox()
    layout.addWidget(group_box)
    box_layout = QVBoxLayout()
    group_box.setLayout(box_layout)

    for i, (name, field_info) in enumerate(form_info.fields.items()):
        if isinstance(field_info, FormInfo):
            raise ValueError(
                "Nesting forms within a SingleChoiceNestedForm is not supported."
            )
        box_layout.addLayout(
            single_choice_field_renderer(field_info, level, checked=not i)
        )
    for error in form_info.schema_errors:
        layout.addWidget(_create_named_label(error, "error"))
    return layout

Submodule related to individual form fields.

Fields are used to build up forms and represent semantically distinct items of data. This is entirely analogous to fields used in libraries such as Marshmallow, WTForms or Django Forms. Fields are intended only to be used as attributes of Form classes.

For our purposes, a Field class ties together a Marshmallow field class and a Widget class with additional data for display to the user. The Marshmallow class of a Field effectively defines the underlying datatype and is used by a Form instance to construct a Marshmallow Schema for data validation. Validator functions may also be provided to a Field and these are passed to the Marshmallow field when the Schema is constructed.

The Widget class specified for a Field represents the actual GUI component that should be presented to the user. All usable Field classes provide a default Widget class however the Widget class may also be provided at initialisation time.

def field_info(
    self,
    name: str,
    data: DataType | list[DataType] | None,
    errors: dict[int, list[str]] = {},
) -> FieldInfo:
"""Return a FieldInfo object for this Field.

    Args:
      name: the name of the field
      data: data for pre-population of inputs
      errors: error messages for individual inputs
    """
    header = self.display_name if self.display_name else name
    if data:
        if isinstance(data, list):
            if len(data) != self.length:
                raise ValueError("Number of data items must match Field length.")
            inputs = [self.input(d) for d in data]
        else:
            if self.length != 1:
                raise ValueError("Expected a list of data items.")
            inputs = [self.input(data)]
    else:
        inputs = [self.input() for _ in range(self.length)]
    if len(inputs) != self.length:
        raise ValueError("Number of values provided by `data` is incorrect.")

    return FieldInfo(
        input=inputs,
        errors=errors,
        header=header,
        description=self.description,
    )

A Form object for collection and validation of data.

This class should be sub-classed to add data fields to the form. Any attributes added that are fields.BaseField subclasses are used to define the data collected and validated by the form. The name of each field is taken from the name of attribute.

By default form fields are ordered according to the orderin which they are defined on the class. This can be manually overridden by setting the field_order attribute of the class to an iterable of field names. Fields will then be ordered according to the specified field names with any left over fields following in the default order.

Form sub-classes may optionally have a validate method. If present, this is used as a schema level validator for the Marshmallow Schema of the form.

Forms may be nested via attributes using a NestedForm instance.

def __init_subclass__(cls) -> None:
"""Initialise subclasses with additional attributes.

    When constructing a new Form subclass, this method looks for attributes that are
    Field subclasses and 1) adds a new dictionary `field` attribute containing
    name->attribute mappings and 2) uses the marshmallow method of each field to
    construct a Marshmallow Schema class for data validation.
    """
    super().__init_subclass__()
    marshmallow_attrs: dict[str, marshmallow_fields.Field | Callable] = {}
    cls.fields = {}

    # iter through __dict__ for bases using __mro__ in order to preserve
    # order of fields according to the order they are defined
    for attr_name, attr in chain(
        *(c.__dict__.items() for c in reversed(cls.__mro__))
    ):
        if isinstance(attr, BaseField):
            cls.fields[attr_name] = attr
            marshmallow_attrs[attr_name] = attr.marshmallow()
        elif isinstance(attr, NestedForm):
            cls.fields[attr_name] = attr.form_class.fields
            marshmallow_attrs[attr_name] = marshmallow_fields.Nested(
                attr.form_class._marshmallow_class
            )

    if schema_validator := getattr(cls, "validate", None):
        marshmallow_attrs["schema_validator"] = validates_schema(schema_validator)

    # could have used Schema.from_dict rather than the below but expected function
    # signature is not compatible with the return type of validates_schema
    cls._marshmallow_class = type(
        f"{cls.__name__}Schema", (Schema,), marshmallow_attrs
    )

    data: dict[str, Any] = {},
    errors: FormErrorsType = {},
    schema_errors: list[str] = [],
    header: str | None = None,
    single_choice: bool = False,

"""Return a FormInfo object for this Form."""
    fields: dict[str, FieldInfo | FormInfo] = {}
    for name, field in self._iter_ordered_field_items():
        # below casts differentiate between the expected datastructures
        # for fields and nested forms.
        if isinstance(field, NestedForm):
            nested_errors = cast(FormErrorsType, errors.get(name, dict()))
            fields[name] = field.form_class().form_info(
                data.get(name, dict()),
                errors=cast(FormErrorsType, nested_errors),
                schema_errors=cast(list[str], nested_errors.get("_schema", [])),
                header=field.display_name if field.display_name else name,
                single_choice=isinstance(field, SingleChoiceNestedForm),
            )
        else:
            fields[name] = field.field_info(
                name,
                data.get(name, None),
                errors=cast(dict[int, list[str]], errors.get(name, dict())),
            )
    return FormInfo(
        fields=fields,
        schema_errors=schema_errors,
        header=header,
        single_choice=single_choice,
    )

def process(self, form_info: FormInfo) -> dict[str, Any]:
"""Extract form data from the provided FormInfo object and validate it.

    Args:
      form_info: FormInfo object containing form data
    """
    try:
        data = self._extract_data(form_info)
        return self._marshmallow_class().load(data)
    except MarshmallowValidationError as e:
        # casts below are used to narrow expected return types as many=True is not
        # used by the underlying Marshmallow schema
        errors = cast(dict[str, list[str] | dict[int, list[str]]], e.messages)
        data = cast(dict[str, Any], e.data)
        schema_errors = cast(list[str], errors.pop("_schema", []))
        field_errors = {}
        for key, value in errors.items():
            if isinstance(value, list):
                field_errors[key] = {0: value}
            elif isinstance(value, dict):
                field_errors[key] = value
            else:
                ValueError("Unexpected data in Marshmallow errors")
        raise ValidationError(field_errors, schema_errors, data)

Widget classes primarily provide a uniform interface over an underlying QWidget class. This abstraction allows Field classes to be interoperable with different widgets providing considerable flexibility in form appearance and behaviour.

Widget classes are also able to provide interoperatibility with Fields by inferring appropriate modifications to a QWidget based on Field validators.     for validator in validators:
        if isinstance(validator, validate.Range):
            min_ = validator.min if validator.min is not None else self._default_min
            max_ = validator.max if validator.max is not None else self._default_max
            break
    else:
        min_ = self._default_min
        max_ = self._default_max

    qt_input.setMaximum(max_)

    return qt_input

def remove_container_sync() -> int:
"""Remove the Solidity container.

    If the container does not exist, nothing will happen.
    """
    global _output_thread, _quitting, _return_code
    try:
        container = docker.container.inspect(SOLIDITY_CONTAINER_NAME)
    except NoSuchContainer:
        return _return_code

    logging.info(f"Stopping Docker container ({container})...")
    _quitting = True

    try:
        container.stop()
    except Exception:
        pass
    try:
        container.remove()
    except Exception:
        pass

    if _output_thread:
        # Threads can't join themselves
        if _output_thread.ident != current_thread().ident:
            _output_thread.join()

        _output_thread = None

    return _return_code

def pubsub_broadcast(
    error_topic: str, success_topic: str, *return_value_names: str
) -> Callable:
"""Broadcast success or failure of function via pubsub.

    If the function returns without error, the returned values are sent as arguments to
    the success_topic message.

    Args:
        error_topic: The topic name on which to broadcast errors
        success_topic: The topic name on which to broadcast function result(s)
        return_value_names: The names of each of the returned values
    """

    def wrapped(func: Callable, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> None:
        try:
            result = func(*args, **kwargs)
        except Exception as error:
            _error_occurred(error_topic, error)
        else:
            # Convert result to a tuple of the right size
            if result is None:
                result = ()
            elif not isinstance(result, tuple):
                result = (result,)

            # Make sure we have the right number of return values
            assert len(result) >= len(return_value_names)

            # Send message with arguments
            msg_kwargs = {name: res for name, res in zip(return_value_names, result)}
            pub.sendMessage(success_topic, **msg_kwargs)

    return decorator(wrapped)
